analysis: What changed vs yesterday's briefs: the story flipped overnight from 'calm into the Fed' to a split verdict on the AI trade. The Fed did exactly what was priced (hold at 3.75-4.00%, 10-2, December hike odds now ~83-85%), so rates are not the mover this morning — earnings are. Alphabet and Microsoft reported the same theme with opposite market answers: both are spending at unprecedented scale (Alphabet $51.4B capex in a quarter, Microsoft $45.2B), but Microsoft paired it with an Azure acceleration to 48% and $18.6B of free cash flow, while Alphabet paired a doubling cloud business with a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow (-$9.07B), a search/ads miss, and an $8.7B equity-securities loss (primarily the SpaceX stake, per the CFO on the call). The market's dividing line is now visible: cloud growth alone no longer earns a pass — cash conversion does. That same scrutiny spilled into software (Fortinet -25%, ServiceNow -18% despite raising its outlook), which deepens the year's AI-disruption worry for the sector rather than resolving it. Signal: the Alphabet/Microsoft divergence and the software slide. Noise: the oil pullback on the reported Vance letter to Tehran is a single reported diplomatic overture, not a deal — WTI is still above $101 and the prior session's geopolitical premium has only partly unwound. Into the open, the tape funnels into 8:30 a.m. ET GDP/PCE (a hot print feeds the December-hike narrative the Fed just kept alive) and the after-close Amazon/Intel prints.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures split into the open: Nasdaq 100 futures -0.99%, S&P 500 futures -0.24%, Dow futures +0.58% as of 5:34 a.m. ET, with Alphabet dragging tech lower while the Dow's lower tech weight cushions it.
headlines.why_it_matters: A tech-led soft open, not broad risk-off — the Dow holding up shows the pressure is concentrated in megacap tech and software.

headlines.headline: Alphabet Q3 miss sinks shares ~10.5% premarket (toward ~$289-292): revenue $127.6B (+25% YoY) just under the ~$128.2B consensus, EPS $2.12 vs ~$3.02 expected, hit by an $8.7B loss on equity securities (primarily the SpaceX stake, per the CFO on the call, cutting EPS by $0.55); Google Cloud more than doubled to $30.7B (+103%, beating ~$29.15B) but Search ($63.4B vs ~$65B) and YouTube ads ($11.2B vs ~$11.4B) missed; capex hit $51.4B and free cash flow was negative $9.07B for a second straight quarter, with ~$200B of 2026 capex and spending set to rise in 2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cloud doubling was not enough — a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow plus an ads miss is repricing Alphabet as a cash-burning builder, and its ~10% drop is the main weight on Nasdaq futures.

headlines.headline: Microsoft beats and rises ~3.5% premarket: fiscal Q1 revenue $92.3B (+19%) vs ~$90.6B expected, adjusted EPS $4.89 vs $4.73, Azure growth accelerated to 48% ($33.2B, vs ~45% expected) with next-quarter Azure guidance of 49-50%; free cash flow was $18.6B despite $45.2B of capex including finance leases.
headlines.why_it_matters: The mirror image of Alphabet — accelerating cloud growth plus positive cash flow is the combination the market is rewarding, making Microsoft the tape's main offset to Alphabet's drag.

headlines.headline: Software slides on earnings: Fortinet -25% (beat Q3 and raised guidance, but product-revenue growth slowed; at least five brokerages cut price targets) and ServiceNow -18% (Q3 profit miss overshadowed a raised full-year subscription outlook); Salesforce -4.3%, Palo Alto Networks -6%, CrowdStrike -5%, Zscaler -5.8% in sympathy.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even beats are being sold when growth decelerates — the software complex is being repriced on AI-disruption fears, and it adds a second leg to tech's soft open.

headlines.headline: Fed held at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 vote (Cook and Hammack dissented for a hike); Chair Warsh gave no forward guidance but announced fewer policy votes from 2027, and traders now price ~83-85% odds of a December hike; the 10-year yield closed near 5.04%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The hold was fully priced, so the live risk is now December — today's GDP and PCE prints at 8:30 a.m. ET feed directly into that hike pricing.

headlines.headline: Oil eases on reported diplomacy: the Wall Street Journal reported Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei to revive peace talks; Brent fell 0.82% to $114.38 and WTI fell 1.24% to $101.51 early Thursday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A reported overture, not a deal — it trims part of the prior session's Houthi-driven premium, but WTI above $101 keeps energy supported.

headlines.headline: Semis soften in sympathy: Nvidia -1%, AMD -3.3%, Intel -3.6% premarket; Marvell fell 9.4% on media reports it is in advanced talks to buy data-center optics maker Lumentum (+4.3%) — neither company has responded to the reports.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed on the Marvell/Lumentum talks — treat that leg as fragile, but the broader chip softness fits the tech-wide de-risking into the open.
